EXPLORATORY_post_hoc_labeled.real_part: REPRODUCED with the regulator: slope of Re S against log((R/pi) sin(pi T0/R)) = 0.1689 (R=50, delta=2), 0.1701 (R=100, delta=5), 0.1705 (R=100, delta=10) against 1/6 = 0.1667: within 2-3 percent, two-parameter form confirmed.
EXPLORATORY_post_hoc_labeled.imaginary_part: NOT REPRODUCED. abs(Im S) <= 0.017 over the window at every delta from 2 to 50, sign flipping with delta, and <= 0.0014 on the stable small-T0 region; the prediction is pi/12 = 0.2618. No approach toward pi/12 with increasing delta at c = 1/2.

key_findings: 1. The Gaussian route is an exact evaluation of the transition-matrix definition for the TFIM (spectrum identity to 1e-11); there is no lattice prescription in this construction, unlike the continuum-dispersion substitution of PAPER-139.
2. Im S == 0 EXACTLY for the literal object exp(iRH) on the critical TFIM, by the chiral symmetry V H V(dag) = -H. Proven and verified. This holds for every R, T0, L.
3. With the regulator exp(-delta H), the REAL part of the timelike entanglement entropy follows (c/3) log((R/pi) sin(pi T0/R)) at c = 1/2 in both parameters, to 2-3 percent (exploratory, L = 1024).

4. With the same regulator the IMAGINARY part stays at the 1e-2 level or below and does not approach pi c/6 up to delta = 50 (exploratory). At c = 1/2 on this lattice, Im S = i pi c/6 is not observed in an exact evaluation of the regulated operator.

5. The pseudo entropy at imaginary temperature is branch-ambiguous on the lattice whenever eigenvalues of tau_A wrap the negative real axis; per-eigenvalue and per-mode principal branches differ by O(1) in Re S. Any lattice claim about Im S must state its branch convention.
